get.summary: List the oauth2 channels the login page offers
get.description: Answers the enabled oauth2 channels with the url that starts their authorization. The route needs no authentication, because it is read by the login page before there is a session.

200.description: The enabled oauth2 channels with their start url.

get.summary: Start the oauth2 authorization of a channel
get.description: Redirects the browser to the authorization endpoint of the channel. The route needs no authentication, because it is the way into the administration and not a call of it.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The technical name of the channel the administrator logs in with.

302.description: The browser is sent to the authorization endpoint of the channel.

400.description: The channel is unknown or not configured. The answer is the error page of the login, not the api error envelope.

get.summary: Answer the oauth2 authorization of the administration login
get.description: Reads the identity the channel answered, resolves the administrator that is bound to it and opens the session. The route needs no authentication, because the session is what it creates.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: The technical name of the channel the administrator logs in with.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code the channel answered with.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The state that was sent to the channel and has to come back unchanged.

302.description: The session was opened and the browser is sent to the administration.

400.description: The answer of the channel is invalid, expired or belongs to no administrator. The answer is the error page of the login, not the api error envelope.
